hesitation-is-normal.description: Computer anxiety is a long-studied, widespread reaction; about 80% of the 89 studies on experience found more experience went with less anxiety, and a relaxed first experience was linked to lower anxiety. No study measures fear of the terminal itself, so applying this to the terminal is an inference [1].

powell-computer-anxiety.title: Powell, Computer anxiety: Comparison of research from the 1990s and 2000s

why-the-command-line-feels-scary.header: Why the command line feels scary
why-the-command-line-feels-scary.description: System administrators said you cannot click your way around a command line to figure it out, and that it may be scary or overwhelming for a beginner; this is a survey quote, not a measured rate of mistakes [1].

voronkov-sysadmins-cli.title: Voronkov, Martucci and Lindskog, System Administrators Prefer Command Line Interfaces, Don't They? An Exploratory Study of Firewall Interfaces

setup-is-the-hard-part.description: Software Carpentry reports that installing software is often harder than using it, and that every new tool fails for at least one person in the room across Mac, Windows and Linux [1].

feedback-builds-confidence.description: In a university Unix course with near-instant per-answer feedback, 78.2% of 2021 respondents said they had procedural Unix knowledge, against 38.8% before; the authors call this self-report possibly subjective, and the students were not solo first-timers [1].

berry-shellonyou.title: Berry et al., ShellOnYou: learning by doing Unix command line

not-a-personal-failing.title: Not a personal failing
not-a-personal-failing.script: If opening a terminal feels a little odd, that is a common reaction, and I would not read it as a sign that you are bad with computers. I think the fear comes from the blank window that gives you no hint what to press, and that is my hypothesis, not a proven fact. Nothing here asks you to prove anything, we only open the window and look at it.

one-window-one-cursor.title: One window, one cursor
one-window-one-cursor.script: Pick your system in the toolbar, then find Terminal on a Mac, PowerShell on Windows, or the terminal on Linux, and open it. You will see a mostly empty window with a blinking cursor, and that is exactly what success looks like here. It is not frozen, it is waiting for you.

stuck-paste-it.title: Stuck? Paste it
stuck-paste-it.script: If something looks different on your screen, you do not have to work it out alone. Paste your error into the troubleshooting box under the step, and it wraps your system, your AI agent and the step number into a prompt you can hand to a free ChatGPT. Every step below has one, so asking for help is part of the route.
